title: PowerMove: Optimizing Compilation for Neutral Atom Quantum Computers with Zoned Architecture
problem: Neutral atom quantum computers (NAQCs) with zoned architectures (ZA) and qubit movement capabilities require coordinated gate scheduling, qubit positioning, atom movement, and inter-zone communication, but existing compilers cannot jointly optimize these dimensions, leading to poor fidelity and long execution times for quantum circuits.
motivation: NAQCs have emerged as leading platforms for scalable quantum computing due to hardware-native qubit movement and zoned architecture capabilities, but without compilers that exploit these features, the hardware advantages translate to poor circuit performance in practice.
method: PowerMove is a compiler for NAQCs that jointly optimizes gate scheduling, qubit positioning, atom movement, and inter-zone communication for zoned architectures. The compiler introduces new optimization passes that model atom movement as a first-class resource and explore movement strategies jointly with gate ordering. For NISQ applications, PowerMove significantly reduces the number of atom movements and inter-zone communications, while for FTQC (fault-tolerant quantum computing), it replaces physical qubits with logical qubits encoded in quantum error correction (QEC) codes and applies analogous optimization. The compilation algorithm is designed for both correctness and efficiency, achieving up to 216.9x compilation speedup over prior methods.
key_novelty: Jointly optimizing atom movement strategies alongside gate scheduling and qubit positioning for both NISQ and FTQC settings in neutral atom zoned architectures, achieving orders-of-magnitude fidelity improvement.
contributions: PowerMove compiler design jointly optimizing gate scheduling, qubit positioning, atom movement, and inter-zone communication for NAQCs with zoned architecture.
Orders-of-magnitude fidelity improvements over state-of-the-art NAQC compilers.
Up to 3.76x reduction in NISQ circuit execution time and 216.9x compilation speedup.
Extension to FTQC with logical qubits (QEC codes) achieving 4.78x reduction in execution time; open-sourced code.

metrics.speedup: 3.76x execution time reduction (NISQ); 4.78x execution time reduction (FTQC)

baselines: state-of-the-art NAQC compilers for zoned architecture
limitations: The compiler's joint optimization may have scalability limits for very large circuits or many qubits; specific resource (connectivity, move latency) assumptions are tied to current NAQC hardware generations.
primary_theme: joint atom-movement-aware compilation for neutral atom quantum computers
